chapter: Chapter 6 — Measuring What Matters (Figure 6.2, printed page 128)
evidence: Rendered figure art on PDF p.152 (printed p.128) shows annotation labels drawn on top of each other: 'p50 0.80', 'p90 0.94' and 'p95 0.99' are stacked at the same position with 'p99 = 1.33 s' overlapping them; 'mean = 0.85s', 'sample p99 (interpolation) = 1.33s' and 'population p99 = 5.0 s' overlap in one illegible cluster; 'SLO-violating region (> 2 s)' overlaps 'SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)' and '1% stragglers', and '~5 s (cross the SLO)' overlaps that cluster. The caption — 'figure 6.2: Request-latency distribution: the mean looks healthy and the p95 SLO is met (p95 ≈ 0.99 s ≤ 2 s), while 1% of requests exceed the 2 s request-latency line…' — acknowledges only one art erratum ('the in-figure blue threshold label reads SLO 2 s (TTFT budget) — an erratum in the figure art'), not the label collisions.
issue: Figure 6.2's annotation layout collides: at least seven annotation labels overlap in two piles, making the percentile annotations (p50/p90/p95/p99) and the mean/sample-p99/population-p99 callouts illegible in the rendered figure. The underlying data and all caption values are correct (verified from the chapter's own inputs: two-point mean 0.99×0.8+0.01×5 = 0.842 s; mixture mean 0.99×0.8058+0.01×5 ≈ 0.848 s; sample mean 0.85 s; interpolated sample p99 = 1.30 + 0.01×(5.0−1.30) = 1.337 → displayed 1.33 s as a stated truncation), so this is a figure-art/layout defect only — but it defeats the figure's teaching purpose, which is reading percentiles off the distribution.
fix_instruction: Regenerate Figure 6.2 with non-overlapping annotation placement: spread the p50/p90/p95/p99 percentile labels vertically beside their respective percentile lines, move the mean/sample-p99/population-p99 callout box to an empty region of the plot (e.g. upper right), and separate the SLO-violating-region, SLO-line and straggler-cluster labels; keep all printed values and the existing caption erratum note unchanged.
